pr_title: ILLink analyzer: add warnings for DAM on type
pr_body:
Implements analyzer warnings for DynamicallyAccessedMembers annotations on types.
The warnings are generated the same way ILLink does in "library mode" - so the presence of DAM on a type is sufficient to warn on any referenced members that have RUC or DAM annotations. It doesn't need object.GetType() to be called on an instance of a derived type.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/104742
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/102002

Depends on https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/105956

issue_context.title: ILLink: Trim analyzer doesn't warn on reflection access to annotated members when the source of the `Type` is GetType on a DAM-annotated class

review_comments: Why don't we only apply the missing DAMT like we do for the base type?

We do only apply the missing DAMT, but the logic is a little different because only All or Interfaces needs to be applied to interfaces in the first place. The `HasFlag` check a few lines above this is doing the check for missing DAMT.
Do we need to worry about what happens if code ref emits? It seems like all bets are off if the code uses ref emit.

Ref emit isn't necessarily trim-incompatible, though I'm not familiar with the details. The point of the comment (copied from the same logic for linker/ILC) is that ref-emit which calls an annotated method will generate warnings at the point that gets the reference to that method.
